sources: AccessPediatrics IUGR — ponderal index for soft-tissue mass vs skeletal development / asymmetric IUGR
Woolcott & Bergman 2018 — RFM = 64 − 20×(height/waist) + 12×sex; better DXA %fat estimate than BMI
Ashwell / WHtR 0.5 — 'keep waist less than half height'; common cardiometabolic screening cut-off
Krakauer 2012 — ABSI (WC independent of BMI) associates with mortality hazard
Valdez conicity — theoretical range ~1.0 (cylinder) to 1.73 (double cone); higher = more central mass
Katch–McArdle BMR = 370 + 21.6×LBM(kg); LBM-based, no age/sex/height once LBM known
Roza AM, Shizgal HM. Am J Clin Nutr. 1984 — revised Harris–Benedict BMR × activity factor = TDEE workflow
Standard pediatrics fluid teaching — deficit (L) ≈ wt(kg)×(% dehydration/100); separate maintenance and ongoing losses
Common pediatric maintenance teaching ~2–3 mEq/kg/day Na and ~1–2 mEq/kg/day K (disease-adjusted)
Common US practice: peripheral ~10 mEq/h and premixed ~10 mEq/100 mL; institutional policies vary
NS 154, LR 130, ½NS 77 mEq/L Na; continuous 3% often central-preferred by policy (peripheral increasingly studied)
ASPEN — PPN osmolarity up to ~900 mOsm/L generally preferred for peripheral vein
Term neonatal target GIR often ~4–6 mg/kg/min; adjust for hypo/hyperglycemia; high GIR + hypoglycemia → hyperinsulinism workup
ADA DKA pathways — typical insulin infusion often 0.1 U/kg/hr; K/glucose monitoring; overlap basal before stopping drip
Standard ICU drip math: mL/hr = (mcg/kg/min × kg × 60) / (mcg/mL)
Reverse of standard vasoactive drip conversion for handoff/order check
Nursing standard: gtt/min = (volume_mL × drop factor) / time_min; pumps preferred for critical meds
Pharmacy identity C₁V₁ = C₂V₂ for liquid dilutions with consistent concentration units
Siggaard-Andersen / van Slyke-style BE from pH and HCO₃; analyzers use fuller hemoglobin models
Bedside mnemonic expected PaO₂ ≈ FiO₂% × 5; crude gas-exchange screen vs measured ABG
Tanaka 2001 — HRmax ≈ 208 − 0.7×age; often preferred to 220 − age in healthy adults
BTS — most acutely ill 94–98%; COPD/hypercapnia risk often 88–92% with controlled O₂ and ABG
Liu 2012 — MSI = HR/MAP; elevated MSI associated with ICU/mortality; may outperform SI in some cohorts
